intro: Energy enters an ecosystem as sunlight, is stored by producers and passes up the food chain one feeding step at a time; at every step most of it leaves as heat. Three chapters: drag the energy up a meadow's pyramid and watch 90% leave at each step; feed a hectare of corn to cattle and count the people it still feeds; take a species out of a food web and see who answers.
howItWorks:
The producers capture gross primary productivity (GPP) and use part of it in their own cellular respiration; what is left is net primary productivity: NPP = GPP − respiration. Level n of the chain holds NPP × 0.1n − 1 kcal/m²/yr with the 10% rule. Every value comes from the same calculation recipes the question bank uses.

Eat lower: a hectare of corn grows about 40 million kcal of grain a year (USDA yields), a person eats about 2,500 kcal a day, and grain fed to cattle passes one more step at 10%.

In the food web, removing a species shows its first, most likely effects: a consumer whose only food is gone dies out, the removed species' prey increase, and its predators decrease. Indirect effects (a hungry predator eating more of another food) are marked as less certain. The biomass and numbers pyramids of a grassland, a pond and a forest are in “?”.
